name: Qin and Han Dynasties
summary: Qin and Han Dynasties is the historical imperial aesthetic of China from 221 BCE to 220 CE.
description: Qin and Han Dynasties is the historical imperial aesthetic of China from 221 BCE to 220 CE.
culturalContext: Under Construction, In 221 BC, the Qin Dynasty established a centralized governing system. Craftsmen had to work at official state workshops, while the overall economy was constrained, so the general public didn’t have the money or manpower to do artistic creation. Additionally, the Qin Dynasty only existed for 14 years. Thus the most notable works of art were all created on the orders of the First Emperor of Qin. The first emperor of Han, Liu Bang (256 or 247 – 1 June 195 BC), liked Chu music. Because of this, the Han Dynasty also brought in art styles of Chu from pre-Qin times. The design of Han-dynasty lacquerware is believed to be shaped by these arts. Improvements in textile-making skills during the Han Dynasty brought about gorgeous silk fabrics. The Han Dynasty’s economy flourished like never before, spawning big private landed estates and bustling markets. After the Rule of Wen…

fashion.Overview: Under Construction, Fashion of the Qin and Han dynasties centred around various forms of pao (袍) robes. The shenyi (深衣) robe was the most common and important garment, initially a daily outfit but evolved into formal ceremonial wear. The quju (曲裾) shenyi was common in the Western Han while the zhiju (直裾) shenyi was popular in the Eastern Han. Noble women favoured the duoma-ji (堕马髻) hairstyle, a tilted bun that hangs to one side. Various guan hats displayed men's social status and rank. Jacquard brocades with complex structures is common due to advancements in loom technology.
